assumptions.summary: The coauthor graph is treated as undirected after the minor adjacency asymmetry is repaired.
Shortest-path distances and a stress-majorization layout represent network geometry.
Betweenness is based on equiprobable shortest paths, with a simplified indicator used for runtime.
Citation direction is i cites j; co-bibliography and co-citation are interpreted separately.
Modified Katz uses diminishing-return exponent p and baseline b for uncited new papers.
A singer/songwriter relation can transmit a useful signal, while actor/movie popularity may not.
Ten random five-edge edits and local p/b checks are treated as sensitivity evidence, not full uncertainty.

summary promises a sequence of network decisions rather than a catalogue: State the hidden-champion question, rank researchers, choose paper importance, test transfers, and reserve sensitivity for the end.

an open question becomes a numbered analytical task: Name why a hidden champion is difficult to see, state the network setting, and divide the work into graph, ranking, citation, transfer, and robustness tasks.

a small input defect is repaired visibly before modeling: Detect the asymmetric adjacency entry, state the max repair, retain the undirected coauthor interpretation, and mark the untested consequence.

a sparse-graph reading triggers a layout model: Read the vertex and average-degree evidence, use a visual layout to expose components, and distinguish intrinsic high-degree clutter from a display defect.

a physical analogy becomes an iterative stress calculation: Define distance and stress, replace the hard objective with a solvable surrogate, iterate to a tolerance, and use monotonic decrease as a numerical check.

four centralities are introduced as different questions and compared on one population: State what degree, eigenvector, closeness, and betweenness each can see, calculate them on the same graph, and read agreement before naming a candidate.

a paper network rejects an inherited centrality when its flow semantics fail: Make citation direction explicit, explain why path-based closeness or betweenness lacks the required message flow, and select in-degree, eigenvector, and modified Katz instead.

a directed citation graph is transformed in two ways with separate meanings: Define citation adjacency, form co-bibliography and co-citation products, compare their winning papers, and keep their direction of interpretation distinct.

missing-new-paper behavior and repeated citations trigger a modified Katz repair: Identify the default score problem and diminishing-return need, add a baseline term and exponent, normalize each iteration, and compare the chosen paper with other measures.

a successful transfer and a failed transfer identify the condition for reuse: Apply the model to singers, then contrast the clearer songwriter relation with the actor-film result, diagnose the absence of a meaningful bidirectional transmission, and keep the basic actor graph as the fallback.

a rank recommendation is checked against cost and competition: Use centrality to suggest a collaborator, quantify the one-edge search cost, state the six-hour brute-force limit, and avoid pretending the two-author option was solved.
an expensive realistic branch is left open rather than silently approximated: Estimate the two-author runtime, note possible group-bridging behavior, and place game-theoretic analysis in future work.

robustness is split into graph perturbation, convergence, and parameter checks: Perturb a small number of edges, inspect rank deviations, separate solver convergence from p and b threshold scans, and label the resulting interval local.

the conclusion carries its strengths with the limitations that constrain them: Recap cross-centrality consistency and citation support, retain the transfer caveat and data drawbacks, and finish with moderate rather than universal applicability.

results_trace.summary: The coauthor graph has 511 vertices, 1713 edges, average degree 6.70, and a largest 466-vertex component.
The stress layout reports 42 components and a layout that is more informative than a random placement, while high-degree overlap remains.
ALON is first across the four displayed researcher centralities.
Co-bibliography favors Barabasi 1999 while co-citation favors Newman 2003, demonstrating transform-dependent winners.
The singer transfer is coherent, whereas the actor/movie bipartite result is messy and the basic actor graph is retained.
A one-edge newcomer search is estimated at about six hours; the two-author branch at about four months is not solved.
Ten random five-edge edits move the top-five ranks by at most two; p=.993 and b=.09 are local thresholds.
The visually recovered conclusion calls the applications moderately robust and asks caution because drawbacks remain.

The paper moves from coauthor centrality through directed citation methods, transfer failure, computational cost, and local sensitivity.

decisions: which input defect or semantic mismatch triggers a method switch
when a transfer relation can carry influence
whether a rank recommendation is computationally feasible
inputs: coauthor adjacency, graph distances, citation links, singer/songwriter relations, actor/movie relations, newcomer edge choice, edge perturbations, p/b parameters

title: Who Is the Hidden Champion in a Network?
unresolved_questions: The minor adjacency asymmetry is force-repaired with max(a_ij,a_ji), but no sensitivity check shows whether it changes later ranks.
The layout is judged qualitatively; high-degree overlap remains and monotonic stress does not prove a globally useful drawing.
Eigenvector and closeness calculations omit initialization, component handling, normalization, and full convergence detail.
Betweenness assumes equiprobable geodesic flow, and the simplified indicator changes the metric without a matched accuracy comparison.
The claim that ALON leads all four measures is descriptive because no independent importance outcome is supplied.
Replacing two of sixteen paper citations and adding two books creates a selected paper set whose inclusion rule and edge provenance are not reproducibly documented.
Co-bibliography and co-citation are different questions; their two top papers cannot be used as interchangeable evidence of importance.
Modified Katz lacks a solver trace, initialization policy, missing-paper data protocol, and broad parameter uncertainty beyond its local scan.
Singer, songwriter, actor, and film data sources, membership rules, and credibility outcomes are not documented sufficiently for transfer validation.
The actor-film bipartite result is described as messy, and Table 16 mixes the actor/movie labels; this is evidence against an unqualified transfer claim.
A brute-force one-edge search takes about six hours, so feasibility limits the recommendation even before competition effects are modeled.
The estimated four-month two-author branch is not computed; group-bridging and game theory remain future work rather than results.
Ten random five-edge additions/deletions and top-five deviations do not provide broad structural uncertainty, while p=.993 and b=.09 are only local thresholds.
The conclusion itself limits applications to moderately robust settings and asks caution because data and transfer drawbacks remain.
